subject: GSoC Mentor Summit - selection for attendance?

messages.author: e1122254667b2874
messages.subject: GSoC Mentor Summit - selection for attendance?
parts:
To whom it may concern:
I and Dr. Claudia Vitolo are GSoC mentors for Ben Ubah ("Data-Driven Exploration of the R Community").

Can someone please speak to how we can apply to attend the Munich GSoC Mentor Summit? I am in the United States (Raleigh, NC USA) and Dr. Vitolo is in the UK (London).
Or, can someone speak to the selection process?

Thank you,
Rick Pack

messages.author: b98e21751c27e8b9
messages.subject: Re: GSoC Mentor Summit - selection for attendance?
parts:
Rick,

This is the first year that the Mentor Summit has been heald anywhere other than (at or near) Google Headquarters in California.

So in part, we don't really know how it will work this year. I'll speak to how it has worked in the (recent) past.

In recent years, and I assume again this year, Google has paid organizations a fixed stipend to allow two mentors from an organization to attend the summit.

I try to attend every year to participate in the summit and help maintain R's relationship with the GSoC team at Google.

Typically, the second mentor to attend has been one of our R project mentors. The process for granting a slot has always been informal, with discussion among the R GSoC administrators.

In past years, there has also been a waiting list for other mentors from an organization to attend, which Google has apportioned via some process which has changed over time, and which has not always been disclosed. For waiting list mentors who get mentor summit slots, Google pays for hotel and the provided meals at the summit, but does not change the travel stipend to the organization.  

Any mentors from an organization who want to attend the summit must be approved by the org administrators.

In some years, R has had an additional mentor (and once two) attend the summit. We have used Google's stipend money when available to reimburse travel expenses for mentors who needed travel help (e.g. couldn't expense the trip to their university or work) in order to defray travel costs for more than two mentors if an additional mentor got a slot from Google to attend.

Regards,

Brian
